ai.title: Remove redundant CLI indentLevel prop
ai.summary: Deleted `indentLevel` prop from `ThinkingBlock`, `ToolBranch`, and `AgentBody` in `cli/src/components`. Subagents are already wrapped in boxes, making the extra left-margin calculation redundant. Width calculations now use base `availableWidth` without subtracting `indentLevel * 2`.

eli5.text: When you run the CLI tool, agent responses that appear nested inside other sections no longer add extra blank space on the left before calculating how wide the text columns should be. The tool used to subtract a left margin from the available width, but since subagents are already boxed and indented, that subtraction was double-counting the space. If you looked closely at the output, text and code blocks in these nested areas will sit at the same left edge as before, but they now get a tiny bit more room to use before wrapping or being cut off.

ai.title: Remove keyboard hints for open/close and esc/ctrl-c
ai.summary: Removed '←→ open/close •' and 'Esc/^C skip' from `KEYBOARD_HINTS` in `cli/src/components/ask-user/constants.ts`. Retained '↑↓ navigate •' and 'Enter select'. This simplifies the ask-user prompt UI by stripping deprecated or redundant navigation shortcuts.

eli5.text: When you use the command-line tool and are asked to pick from a list of options, the small text hints showing extra keyboard shortcuts have been trimmed down. You will still see that the up and down arrow keys let you move through the options and Enter confirms your choice, but the hints telling you about left-right open/close and Esc or Ctrl-C to skip have been removed. This only affects people using the command-line version of the tool today.

ai.title: Release 1.0.550 adds CLI mode flags, ask-user accordion, message
ai.summary: Version 1.0.550 ships CLI improvements: new --lite, --max, and --plan flags that set the initial AgentMode via cli/src/index.tsx, message pagination with a LoadPreviousButton and 15-message default batch size, and a batched message updater that flushes every 100ms with guaranteed interval cleanup. The ask-user form was redesigned into a single-screen accordion layout, removing confirm-screen.tsx, other-text-input.tsx, progress-indicator.tsx, and question-header.tsx while adding accordion-question.tsx and question-option.tsx, with focused options now using theme.primary background. Additional changes include a CopyIconButton on user message headers in cli/src/components/message-block.tsx and a shared constants module in cli/src/components/ask-user/constants.ts.
ai.evidence: The diff shows a version bump in cli/release/package.json from 1.0.549 to 1.0.550 (commit c9bd2b98, release-bump). The 1.0.550 release includes user-visible CLI improvements per the same-day commit sequence: CLI flags --lite --max --plan set initial agent mode via cli/src/index.tsx flowing through App to Chat; CLI message pagination with LoadPreviousButton (cli/src/components/load-previous-button.tsx, chat.tsx visibleMessageCount/hiddenMessageCount, batch size 15); CLI batched message updater

eli5.text: Release 1.0.550 gives you faster, cleaner control of Freebuff right from your terminal, with new ways to start conversations, ask questions, and review long chat histories. You can now launch Freebuff in a specific mode from the command line using new flags: --lite for a speedier lightweight session, --max for heavy-duty work, and --plan when you want the agent to think through a problem before acting. When Freebuff asks you follow-up questions, they all appear together in a single expandable accordion panel instead of a step-by-step wizard, so you can review and change your answers at a glance, and clicked follow-up suggestions now populate the input box for your review rather than sending automatically. Long conversations now load gradually with a Load Previous button and smoother streaming, so scrolling back through dozens of messages stays snappy instead of choking your terminal. A new Copy button sits next to every user message so you can grab text or commands in one click, and the ask-user form now gives you clearer keyboard hints and better focus handling so navigating options by mouse or keyboard feels consistent. Upgrading means terminal sessions start exactly how you want them, question prompts are easier to scan and edit, and chatting with the agent stays responsive even as your project grows. In short, you get a quicker, more predictable command-line experience with finer-grained control over how the agent runs and answers you.

ai.title: Block specific user ID from chat completions API
ai.summary: Added `BLOCKED_USER_IDS` check in `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts` to reject requests from a specific user ID. Returns a 503 `upstream_timeout` error to mask the block. Scope limited to the chat completions API endpoint.

eli5.text: A specific user who has been disputing charges is now blocked from using the chat completions API. When that user tries to use the service, they will receive a generic 503 'Overloaded. Request could not be processed' error instead of their usual response. This appears to be a targeted block on one particular user account, implemented so the restriction looks like a temporary service issue rather than an intentional ban.

ai.title: Update base2 system prompt to use askuser tool
ai.summary: The base2 agent system prompt was updated to explicitly instruct the use of the `ask_user` tool for important decisions or guidance. This replaces the generic instruction to 'stop and ask' with a specific tool invocation, emphasizing context gathering first. The change applies to `.agents/base2/base2.ts`.

eli5.text: When you're working with an AI assistant on a coding task, the assistant used to be told to 'stop and ask' you for guidance when it got stuck or needed clarification. Now, the instructions have been updated so the assistant is specifically told to use a dedicated 'ask user' interaction to check in with you. Instead of just saying it should pause for your input, it's now guided to actively reach out to you using this new method, making it clearer when and how you'd be pulled into the conversation to help make decisions or resolve confusion. This change affects how the AI assistant interacts with you during development tasks, encouraging earlier and more intentional check-ins.

ai.title: Fix tool block reordering in CLI UI
ai.summary: Refactored `moveSpawnAgentBlock` in `cli/src/utils/message-block-helpers.ts` to preserve block order. Added `checkBlockIsUnderParent` to detect existing nesting, preventing unnecessary extraction and re-appending. Updates in place if the block is already under the correct parent or if no parent is specified. Covers CLI UI message rendering.

eli5.text: When you run a chat command in the terminal, the assistant's reply shows up as stacked text blocks. Sometimes a block meant to live inside another block (like a sub-step inside a bigger task) was being pulled out and re-stuck to the bottom of the screen, scrambling the order. Now the command checks first whether that block is already sitting in the right spot; if it is, it simply refreshes the text in place instead of dragging it around, so the layout stays where you expect it.

ai.title: CLI followup suggestions send directly with input preserved
ai.summary: Followup suggestion clicks now call `onSubmitPrompt` directly with `preserveInputValue: true` instead of `setInputValue`. Previous behavior only filled the input box; new behavior dispatches the prompt while retaining the user's current input text. Scope limited to `cli/src/chat.tsx` and `cli/src/components/tools/suggest-followups.tsx`. Hover state logic in `FollowupLine` updated to require `!isClicked`.

eli5.text: When you click on a suggested followup question in the CLI chat, it now immediately sends that suggestion as your message while keeping any text you had already typed in the input box. Previously, clicking a suggestion only copied it into the input field, requiring you to press enter separately to send it. The click also now properly prevents the hover effect from appearing on items that have already been clicked. This makes using suggested followups faster and feels more like the suggestion was sent right away rather than staged for you to confirm.
